messages.subject: geom_density with weighted data
parts:
All,

ggplot is awesome.  I would like to plot on a single graph a continuous variable (e.g., IQ) by gender. Unfortunately, my data have non-1 survey weights.  When using weights, I get an error:

Warning messages:
1: In density.default(data$x, adjust = adjust, kernel = kernel, weight = data$weight,  :
  sum(weights) != 1  -- will not get true density
2: In density.default(data$x, adjust = adjust, kernel = kernel, weight = data$weight,  :
  sum(weights) != 1  -- will not get true density

Clearly, within each gender, weights don't add to 1.  I can calculate weights per gender group, as shown below. Is there a better way?

library(ggplot2)
N=100
gender=factor(round(runif(N),0))
levels(gender)=c("Male", "Female")
surveyweight=runif(N)
IQ=80+runif(N)*40

df=data.frame(cbind(gender,IQ,surveyweight))
head(df)

p=ggplot(data=df,aes(x=IQ,color=factor(gender)))
p + geom_density() + labs(title="Unweighted", color="Gender")

df$surveyweight[df$gender==1]=df$surveyweight[df$gender==1]/sum(df$surveyweight[df$gender==1])
df$surveyweight[df$gender==2]=df$surveyweight[df$gender==2]/sum(df$surveyweight[df$gender==2])

tapply(df$surveyweight, gender, sum)

p=ggplot(data=df,aes(x=IQ,weight=surveyweight,color=factor(gender)))
p + geom_density() + labs(title="Weighted", color="Gender")
